slides.title: Everything is on your phone
bullets: Your phone is your character sheet, your evidence file, and your conscience — keep it on you all night.
The tabs across the top hold who you are, your conversations, your map, your role, and your clues — each one arrives when the night needs it.
When the main screen gives an instruction, it outranks whatever you were doing. Even gossip.
slides.braun_says: Everything you need tonight is on the device in your hand. I've put my entire evening on there — my guests, my secrets, my house. Do try not to drop it in the champagne.

slides.title: Who you are tonight
bullets: Tonight you are the person on your screen — their name, their job, their voice, their grudges.
Read your backstory. It's yours to perform, embellish, and weaponize — and it's what you'll say when Braun calls your name.
Your secrets are real. Guard them like money, spend them like money.
slides.braun_says: I've taken the liberty of deciding who each of you really is. Some of you are exactly who you appear to be. The rest of you — well. That's rather the point of the evening.

slides.title: Not everyone here is a guest
bullets: Not everyone here is a simple guest — some of you belong to something larger, and it's on your Role tab from the moment the house needs you to know.
Your faction tells you what you know, who you can trust, and what winning means for you tonight. Each one is explained next — so everybody knows what everybody else might be.
Every power comes live the moment the house reaches the study, and stays live to the end. If you don't see one on your phone, it isn't yours.
slides.braun_says: Every party has its little societies — the loyal, the desperate, the ones taking notes. Tonight, yours comes with instructions. Check your role in private. Then lie about it in public, as is traditional.

slides.title: The Syndicate Hand
bullets: Three of you, one murder. You know each other, and you know how it was done — get one story straight before anyone asks.

One shared power, any time after the murder. Stand at any clue card, scan it, and choose who your story points at. Then choose one of two. Plant: that guest's belongings are written into the card, half-hidden in the scene, for everyone who scans it after you. Scrub: the card is wiped — anyone scanning it after you finds only a disturbed scene and the certainty that someone got there first.

Plant frames somebody; Scrub destroys evidence, but announces there was some. Either way, whoever scanned the card before you keeps the original, and all three of your answers change to put that guest near the study. The card shows you what it would say before you commit. You win if at least two of you are still free after the final trial.
slides.braun_says: Some of my guests have done something terrible, together, and are about to be very good at lying about it. I mention this only so the rest of you know what you're up against.

slides.title: Syndicate Associates
bullets: Two of you. You know all three of the Syndicate's hands; nobody else at this party knows you.
One shared power, any time after the murder: on your Role tab, Take the Blame. If the room then convicts you, your card reads KILLER and counts as one — a hand walks free in your place.
You win with the Syndicate.
slides.braun_says: Every criminal enterprise has its associates — the ones who made the noise and carried the messages. They protect the hands. The hands, I'm told, do not always return the favour.

slides.title: The Investigators
bullets: Three of you, and you can trust each other completely. Each of you carries one tool, and your Role tab says which.
Forensics — two of you have it, once each: choose a card you've scanned and learn whether it was untouched, planted, or scrubbed.

The Hard Question — one of you has it, once: choose a guest and learn KILLER or NOT A KILLER. Both are live from the study on; the answers land under Interactions, and the three of you decide together when to spend them.
slides.braun_says: There are people here who are paid to notice things. Three of them, by my count. They have more tools than the rest of you — and every innocent they hang is a gift to the guilty.

slides.title: The Desperate
bullets: You work alone, and you want the room to convict you. Infamy is the only thing this evening gives away free.
Incriminate Yourself, once, any time after the murder: stand at one clue card, scan it, and choose Subtle or Blatant — your own belongings appear in that card, and your answers start confessing.
You win if the room sends you down at any trial.
slides.braun_says: And one or two of you — I won't say who — would rather be famous than free. Do bear that in mind when somebody is confessing a little too readily.

slides.title: The Braun Claim
bullets: Two of you, rivals for everything James leaves behind. You know exactly who the other is.
Family Secrets, once, any time after the murder: on your Role tab, choose a guest — you receive what a third party says about them behind their back. Ammunition, not proof; make it sound like proof.
You win if your rival is convicted at a trial and you never are.
slides.braun_says: Then there is the small matter of my estate, and the two people with a legal path to it. An estate divides much more cleanly by one. They have both done the arithmetic.

slides.title: Guests of the House
bullets: Most of the room. No powers, no secret allies, nothing to hide — which tonight makes you the most honest people in the building.
Scan the cards, scan the people, star the answers that matter, and compare notes with anyone who'll stand still.
You win with the town: at least two of the Syndicate's three hands convicted by the end of the final trial, and never you.
slides.braun_says: The rest of you are simply my guests: invited for dinner, trapped in a murder. You have no tricks. You have each other, and your eyes. Use both.

slides.title: Nine cards, hidden in the house
bullets: Nine clue cards are hidden through the house, one to a room, each waiting at a spot worth searching.
Scan a card and its evidence goes into your phone — permanently, and only for those who've scanned it.
Evidence can be planted, and evidence can be scrubbed. Trust the cards. Verify the cards.
slides.braun_says: I've hidden nine cards in this house, and I flatter myself they're hidden well. Everything my home witnessed tonight is on them. If anything should happen to me — and it won't — do read my house's testimony carefully.

slides.title: The house, and where the cards are
bullets: Nine rooms, nine cards. There is one card hidden somewhere in each room — the map on your phone shows the rooms, and the searching is up to you.
The study is roped off. Its card is the scene itself, and you'll see it when the house is ready to show you.
slides.braun_says: My house, as you'll find it. I've been generous in every room. The study is mine and mine alone — that door stays shut, and I'd take it as a personal insult if anyone tested it before I do.

slides.title: Scan the people you meet
bullets: Everyone's code is on their phone. Scan somebody's and the two of you are in a conversation: three questions each, taking turns, scanner asks first.
Everything you're told is saved under Interactions. Star what matters.
slides.braun_says: Introductions at my parties are mandatory and now, I'm pleased to say, electronic. Point your phone at somebody's, collect my guests. I acquired most of them the same way — one favor at a time.

slides.title: How somebody goes to jail
bullets: Three trials tonight. The room accuses, the four most suspected take the stand, the jury questions them, and everyone votes. The top two go down.
Anyone may lie, anywhere — on the stand included. Nobody is obliged to tell the truth; catching them at it is the game.
Convictions are permanent, and the convicted lose their vote. Choose like it counts, because it does.
slides.braun_says: Should this evening require justice, it will be served the way I serve everything: publicly, dramatically, and in courses. Three trials. Whoever you convict stays convicted — so do be sure. Or be persuasive.

slides.title: First, introductions
bullets: Before anything else, the room meets itself. Braun goes round everybody, one at a time, and the screen shows whose turn it is.
When it's you: stand, say your name, your age, man or woman, and the 'Who you are' paragraph from your phone.
Listen. Three of you are murderers.
slides.braun_says: Enough instruction. Before the drinks, the introductions — I like to know exactly who is in my house. When I say your name, stand up and tell the room who you are. I'll go first, naturally. It is my house.
